reuse.why: Introduces getExpectedScheduleAmount in shared/schedules.ts, reuses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance and rebases getScheduledAmount on it, but three server sites keep their own missing/number dispatch instead of calling the existing getScheduledAmount that already decides all cases.

duplication.why: The midpoint copies are gone, yet updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions still each re-implement the null/number dispatch that getScheduledAmount owns, and two overlapping public helpers now express the same rule.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount; expectedAmount is attached in the api.ts handler with a separate list type rather than in scheduleModel.toExternal, which is acceptable but splits the API mapping.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and the API field; the Balance.tsx comment tweak and release notes are minor.

maintainability.why: One definition for the core rule is good, but the op-aware rule only reaches callers that pass the operator (desktop-client callers of getScheduledAmount and updateActions' number branch never see isapprox), and a stale 'furthest-from-zero' comment remains in the preview code.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts updateActions returns numeric amounts before calling getExpectedScheduleAmount (skipping the isapprox rule); desktop-client getScheduledAmount calls (SchedulesTable, Balance, SchedulesListItem, MobileSchedulesPage, useScheduleEdit) pass no op; three server sites keep their own null dispatch instead of getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: Remaining duplicates are the sites' original null/number ternaries left in place, not reshaped copies.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter and the shared helper an isapprox branch; updateActions plus seven desktop-client getScheduledAmount calls do not pass the operator, so they bypass the approximate rule.
